title: You Can See Everything crosses $100M US worldwide at the box office

image.caption: Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes appears in a still from the documentary You Can See Everything, which crossed $100 million US at the worldwide box office over the weekend. (A24)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

As Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything makes its way into cinemas around the globe, the buzzy documentary is proving a big-screen draw with international audiences, too, taking in more than $100 million US at box offices worldwide.
Buzzy doc rising on list of top-grossing documentaries ever
As Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything makes its way into more cinemas around the globe, the buzzy documentary is proving a draw with international audiences, too.
The nearly three-hour doc has now grossed more than $102.4 million US worldwide, according to cinema revenue tracker Box Office Mojo.
That includes netting the largest ever opening in the United Kingdom for a non-music documentary this past weekend.
Directed by Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the doc begins in the weeks before Theranos founder and convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes began her 11-year prison term for defrauding investors.
Nathan Fielder searches for truth in You Can See Everything

Since opening in mid-October, the doc has earned nearly $93.5 million US at the domestic box office (U.S. and Canada) and about $9 million US in international markets, where the A24 film has had a staggered rollout across eastern Europe, Australia and New Zealand in the weeks since its premiere.
In the coming weeks, the movie is slated to hit theatres in a raft of new territories, including Mexico, South America and a wider swath of European and Asian countries.

items: Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything gazes into the abyss of Elizabeth Holmes

blocks.text: A24 has also launched an ambitious awards season campaign for the film, appealing to industry voters for consideration in multiple categories, including best picture, best director and feature documentary.
Rare doc success

Excluding concert docs, You Can See Everything has made the biggest splash in the overall genre in years. It's scored spectacularly on movie review aggregator site Rotten Tomatoes (a 97 per cent fresh rating) and film-centred social platform Letterboxd (4.6/5) and inspired online memes, parodies and widespread discussion.

items: You Can See Everything is changing how we think about documentaries

blocks.text: Though posthumous Michael Jackson tale This Is It and Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour currently top the list of highest grossing documentaries worldwide ($267.98 million US and $261.66 million US, respectively), success for You Can See Everything has already vaulted it into the top 10.
Continued success could push it higher among the non-musical docs atop that list, though it still has some way to go to upset the current leader: Michael Moore's Fahrenheit 9/11.
Moviegoers queue for Michael Moore's documentary Fahrenheit 9/11 in New York in 2004. It remains the top-grossing non-music documentary in the world. (Don Emmert/AFP via Getty Images)

Since its release in 2004, when it also won the Cannes Film Festival's top prize, Moore's blistering critique of former U.S. president George W. Bush's response to the Sept. 11 attacks has grossed $222.45 million US worldwide.

Other top-grossing, non-music docs include 1998 mountain-climbing short doc Everest, 2005's Antarctic tale March of the Penguins and Earth, a 2007 feature-length version of the successful Planet Earth TV series.
Top 10 highest-grossing documentaries worldwide as of Nov. 23:

items: Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour (2023) — $261,656,269 US.
Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (2011) — $99,036,827 US.
One Direction: This Is Us (2013) — $74,373,313 US.
